result: Wing disc-associated AMPs proliferate from approximately 10 cells at embryonic/early larval stages to approximately 2500 cells by late third instar, with each embryonically born AMP giving rise to a lineage of approximately 250 cells during larval development (C2, C11-C15, C3).
evaluation: The quantitative data showing AMP numbers at different developmental stages (C11-C14) are directly stated and supported by Figure 1. The calculation that each AMP generates ~250 progeny (C15) is mathematically consistent (2500/10=250) and supported by the data. Sample sizes are provided (n=5-20) and error bars are included.

result: AMPs undergo symmetric cell divisions during early larval development (first and second instar, 30-72 hr AEL), with division axes oriented parallel to the wing disc epithelium and cells arranged in a monostratified layer (C4, C16-C17, C21, C27).
evaluation: Twin-spot MARCM experiments (C16, Figure 2A-C) demonstrate equal-sized clones indicative of symmetric divisions. The parallel division axis is supported by CNN-GFP centrosome labeling (C27, Figure 3E-H'). The monostratified arrangement is documented by immunolabeling (C21, Figure 3A-B'). Multiple independent lines of evidence converge on this conclusion.

result: AMPs switch to asymmetric cell divisions from early third instar onward (≥75 hr AEL), with division axes oriented obliquely/orthogonally to the disc surface, resulting in self-renewing stem cells that remain epithelium-adjacent and postmitotic daughters that move to distal layers (C5, C18-C20, C22, C28-C29).
evaluation: Twin-spot MARCM experiments show unequal clones with one large cell and ~10 smaller cells (C18-C19, Figure 2D-F), consistent with asymmetric division. The oblique/orthogonal division axis is documented by CNN-GFP labeling (C28, Figure 3I-L'). The multistratified arrangement (C22, Figure 3C-C') and inference about daughter cell fates (C29) are logically consistent with the division orientation data.

result: Mitotically active cells are restricted to the layer immediately adjacent to the wing disc epithelium throughout larval development, while cells in distal layers are postmitotic progeny, as demonstrated by PH3 labeling, EdU pulse-chase experiments, and MARCM clonal analysis (C23-C26, C30-C35).
evaluation: Multiple independent experimental approaches converge: PH3 immunolabeling shows mitotic cells only in the proximal layer (C23-C24, Figure 3D-D''), EdU pulse-chase shows labeled cells moving from proximal to distal layers over 48 hours (C30-C32, Figure 4A-D), and MARCM clones show only one PH3+ cell per clone always located proximally (C35, Figure 4F-F'). The evidence is internally consistent and well-documented.

result: Notch signaling is required for proliferative activity in AMP lineages throughout larval development, with Notch downregulation reducing mitotic activity by ~50% and Notch overexpression approximately doubling it (C36-C41, C43-C44).
evaluation: NICD expression is documented in all Twi+ cells across all stages (C36-C37, Figure 5A-H). Loss-of-function (RNAi) and gain-of-function (NICD overexpression) experiments show reciprocal effects on PH3+ cell numbers with statistical significance (p<0.001) and appropriate controls (C38, C40, Figure 5D-E). The use of Gal80ts to temporally restrict perturbations strengthens the conclusions. Sample sizes (n=12-20) are adequate.

result: Serrate expressed in the wing disc epithelium acts as a ligand for Notch activation in adjacent AMPs, with epithelial Serrate knockdown reducing mitotic activity by >50%, establishing the disc epithelium as a signaling niche (C45-C50).
evaluation: Serrate-LacZ reporter shows close apposition of Serrate-expressing epithelial cells to AMPs across all larval stages (C45-C46, Figure 6A-H', Video 4). Epithelium-specific Serrate knockdown (using Ap-Gal4) significantly reduces PH3+ cells (C47, Figure 6I, p<0.001, n=15). The inference that epithelial Serrate activates Notch in AMPs (C48-C49) is well-supported by combining Serrate and Notch requirement data. The niche concept (C50) is appropriately cautious.

result: Numb is expressed in AMP lineages specifically during the third instar stage (but not earlier), with strongest expression in distal layers, and is required for the transition from symmetric to asymmetric divisions through downregulation of Notch (C51-C57).
evaluation: While the functional requirement for Numb in asymmetric division is well-supported by twin-spot MARCM experiments showing symmetric clones upon Numb knockdown (C54-C55, Figure 7F-H) and with constitutive Notch activation (C56, Figure 7I-K), a critical weakness is that the temporal expression data for Numb in first/second instars is stated as 'data not shown' (C51). The differential expression pattern in third instar (C52, Figure 7A-D) is documented. The mechanistic model (C57) is logical but the lack of shown data for early stages weakens confidence in the temporal specificity claim.

result: Wingless signaling from the wing disc notum epithelium, expressed from early third instar onwards, is required for Numb expression in AMPs and regulates both the switch to asymmetric division and overall proliferation (C58-C67).
evaluation: The temporal and spatial expression of Wingless is documented by immunolabeling and supported by citations (C58-C60, Figure 8A-H, Video 5). Wingless loss-of-function experiments show complete loss of both beta-catenin (C61-C62, Figure 8I-N) and Numb expression (C63-C64, Figure 8O-V) in all Twi+ cells. Effects on mitotic activity (C65, Figure 9A-J) and division orientation (C66, Figure 9-supplement 2) are documented. The dual effects model (C67) is appropriately presented as a suggestion. Multiple alleles and approaches strengthen the conclusions.

result: The epidermal tissue of the wing imaginal disc acts as a stem cell niche expressing the ligands Serrate and Wingless that regulate AMP proliferation in both symmetric and asymmetric division modes (C9, C83-C84).
evaluation: This integrative conclusion is well-supported by the combined evidence for Serrate (Figure 6) and Wingless (Figure 8) expression in the disc epithelium and their functional requirements for AMP proliferation. The niche concept is appropriate given the spatial restriction of ligands, the contact-dependent nature of signaling, and the restriction of mitotic activity to epithelium-adjacent cells. The claim synthesizes multiple experimental results coherently.

result: The disc-associated AMPs represent a novel muscle stem cell population that orchestrates early adult flight muscle development through sequential symmetric and asymmetric divisions, resulting in architectural changes from monostratified to multistratified organization (C10, C82).
evaluation: This overarching conclusion integrates the demonstrated properties of AMPs: self-renewal capacity, generation of differentiated progeny, niche dependence, and sequential division modes. The architectural transition from monostratified to multistratified arrangement (C82) is directly documented (Figures 3, Video 1). The characterization as 'novel muscle stem cells' (C10) is justified by the stem cell properties demonstrated, though the authors appropriately note the lack of a specific stem cell marker as a limitation in the Discussion.

result: AMPs are embryonically set-aside progenitor cells derived from asymmetric divisions of mesodermal progenitors that remain undifferentiated and associate with imaginal discs, with prior work establishing their role in flight muscle development and the regulatory influence of disc ectoderm (C1, C68-C71, C76-C81).
evaluation: These claims establish the developmental context and prior knowledge about AMPs. They are well-supported by multiple citations to established literature (Currie and Bate 1991, Fernandes et al. 1991, Bate et al. 1991, Roy and VijayRaghavan 1999, Sudarsan et al. 2001, etc.). The claims accurately represent prior work and provide necessary background. The differential proliferation between T2 and T3 segments (C80) and the role of disc ectoderm (C81) set up the key questions addressed in this study.

result: Stem cell populations generally can expand through symmetric divisions or undergo asymmetric self-renewing divisions, with regulation typically occurring through stem cell niches, as exemplified in various Drosophila and vertebrate tissues (C72-C75).
evaluation: These claims provide general background on stem cell biology and are well-supported by multiple authoritative citations (Morrison and Kimble 2006, Knoblich 2001, Egger et al. 2008, 2011, etc.). The optic lobe example (C75) is particularly relevant as it shows a similar transition from symmetric to asymmetric divisions. These claims appropriately contextualize the current findings within the broader stem cell field.

result: In Notch overexpression experiments, mitotically active cells were occasionally seen in more distal cell layers, contrasting with wild-type where mitosis is restricted to the proximal layer (C42).
evaluation: This observation is explicitly stated as 'data not shown' in the manuscript. While the claim may be accurate, the lack of presented data makes it impossible to evaluate the frequency, statistical significance, or robustness of this observation. This represents a missed opportunity to strengthen the mechanistic understanding of how Notch signaling restricts mitotic activity to the proximal layer.
